# Plugin API reference

Preview. This is the contract of user plugins at API 0.1, declarative packages and code packages. Read the [guide](guide.md) first. Names and limits below are enforced by the host; a package that breaks one is refused with the reason.

## Capabilities

A package lists the capabilities it needs in `capabilities` (required) and `optional_capabilities`. The user sees the sentence in the Consent column before installing and decides about each optional one then; a single capability cannot be revoked later. A plugin never sees what a capability excludes.

| Id | Kind | Since | Consent sentence | Not included | Result fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clock.now` | observe | 0.1 | See the current time and your time zone. | A timer finer than a minute. | `unix_minutes`: number, `utc_offset_seconds`: number |
| `workspace.kind` | observe | 0.1 | See what kind of workspace a window shows and whether it is connected. | Title, host, user, path and tab count. | `connected`: bool, `kind`: text |
| `monitor.usage` | observe | 0.1 | See how busy this computer is. | Processes and host names. | `cpu_percent`: number, `memory_percent`: number |
| `transfers.counts` | observe | 0.1 | See how many file transfers are running or failed. | File names, paths and rates. | `active`: number, `failed`: number |
| `notifications.own` | observe | 0.1 | See the notices this plugin posted. | Notices of the host and of other plugins. |  |
| `notifications.post` | effect | 0.1 | Show notices in the status bar. | Actions, links and the error level. |  |
| `panels.set-open` | effect | 0.1 | Open or close its own panels when you click it. | Other contributions and moving focus. |  |
| `panels.set-badge` | effect | 0.1 | Show a number on its own panel or widget. | Attention requests. |  |
| `storage.set` | effect | 0.1 | Keep a small amount of its own data. | Data of other plugins. |  |
| `storage.remove` | effect | 0.1 | Remove its own stored data. | Data of other plugins. |  |

## Manifest keys

A package is one TOML file. Unknown keys are refused. `contribution` and `settings.group` are arrays of tables.

| Table | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| `contribution` | `local`, `kind`, `title`, `icon`, `zone`, `order`, `view` |
| `contribution.view` | `refresh`, `nodes` |
| `contribution.view.nodes` | `kind`, `parent`, `key`, `tone`, `tone_when`, `text`, `icon`, `value`, `each` |
| `manifest` | `api`, `runtime`, `publisher`, `id`, `name`, `description`, `capabilities`, `optional_capabilities`, `reasons`, `contribution`, `settings` |
| `settings` | `version`, `group` |
| `settings.group` | `title`, `contribution`, `field` |
| `settings.group.field` | `key`, `label`, `help`, `kind`, `renamed_from`, `default`, `options`, `ordered`, `max_chosen`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `unit`, `max_len`, `placeholder` |
| `settings.group.field.options` | `key`, `label`, `help` |

### Effect requests

Only a runtime that runs code returns effects; a declarative package cannot. The host lists them so that the capability table stays one list.

| Effect | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `notifications.post` | `tone`, `text`, `notice_key` |
| `panels.set-badge` | `local`, `badge` |
| `panels.set-open` | `local`, `open` |
| `storage.remove` | `key` |
| `storage.set` | `key`, `value` |

| Runtimes | `declarative`, `wasm` |

## Code package ABI

A code package is one WebAssembly module (at most 2097152 bytes) whose custom section `nocterm.manifest` holds the manifest TOML, with `runtime = "wasm"`. The module has no imports: it cannot reach the host except through the call below. ABI version: 1. The golden file `crates/plugin-abi/abi-golden.json` pins the bytes of the wire types, and the host refuses a module whose `nocterm_abi_version` differs.

| Export | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `memory` | `memory` |
| `nocterm_abi_version` | `() -> i32` |
| `nocterm_alloc` | `(i32) -> i32` |
| `nocterm_call` | `(i32, i32) -> i64` |

The host writes a postcard `Call` into a buffer from `nocterm_alloc` and calls `nocterm_call(ptr, len)`; the guest returns `ptr << 32 | len` of a postcard `Reply`. The reply pointer stays valid until the next call.

| ABI limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Call input | 262144 bytes |
| Reply | 262144 bytes |
| Log lines per call | at most 8 |
| Fuel per call | 4000000 |
| Fuel to instantiate | 20000000 |
| Linear memory per instance | 16777216 bytes |
| Live instances | 16 |
